ar.ts.translation.manual.title: (ar) CloudBSD Admin Web UI - User Manual
ar.ts.translation.manual.intro_text: (ar) CloudBSD Admin Web UI is a modern, responsive interface designed for managing infrastructure on FreeBSD and other CloudBSD-compatible systems. It provides a centralized dashboard for monitoring and controlling Virtual Machines (bhyve), OCI-compliant containers, and native FreeBSD Jails.
ar.ts.translation.manual.login_text: (ar) Access the UI at your configured port. Default credentials are admin/admin. It is highly recommended to change the admin password or create a new admin user immediately after first login.
ar.ts.translation.manual.language_text: (ar) On the login page, you can select your preferred language from a dropdown menu in the footer. Your language choice is persisted to your user profile once logged in.
ar.ts.translation.manual.dashboard_text: (ar) The Dashboard provides a real-time overview of your system's health, including CPU and Memory usage, status of running resources, and recent system alerts.
ar.ts.translation.manual.vms_text: (ar) Manage bhyve virtual machines: list configured VMs, control their state (start/stop/restart), and access consoles directly from the web interface.
ar.ts.translation.manual.containers_text: (ar) Monitor and manage OCI-compliant containers (Docker/Podman): view resource consumption and perform basic lifecycle operations.
ar.ts.translation.manual.jails_text: (ar) Manage native FreeBSD Jails: view all active and inactive Jails, and monitor resource isolation.
ar.ts.translation.manual.cluster_text: (ar) The Cluster view allows you to manage multiple nodes within your CloudBSD infrastructure, providing a unified view of resource distribution.
ar.ts.translation.manual.network_map_text: (ar) The Network Map provides a visual representation of your infrastructure's networking, including connections between hosts, VMs, and containers.
ar.ts.translation.manual.roles_admin: (ar) Admin: Full access to all features, including user management and system configuration.
ar.ts.translation.manual.roles_operator: (ar) Operator: Can manage resources (VMs, Containers, Jails) but cannot manage users.
ar.ts.translation.manual.roles_viewer: (ar) Viewer: Read-only access to resources and system stats.
ar.ts.translation.manual.user_management_text: (ar) Administrators can create, edit, and delete users, and assign permissions.
ar.ts.translation.manual.logs_text: (ar) The Logs page provides a searchable audit trail of system activities.
ar.ts.translation.manual.settings_text: (ar) Change user profile information, update language preference, and toggle system settings.
ar.ts.translation.manual.trouble_auth: (ar) Authentication fails: Check configuration for JWT secret keys and ensure the database file is writable.
ar.ts.translation.manual.trouble_lang: (ar) Language not changing: Ensure your browser's local storage is not blocked.

lv.ts.translation.manual.login_text: (lv) Access the UI at your configured port. Default credentials are admin/admin. It is highly recommended to change the admin password or create a new admin user immediately after first login.
lv.ts.translation.manual.language_text: (lv) On the login page, you can select your preferred language from a dropdown menu in the footer. Your language choice is persisted to your user profile once logged in.
lv.ts.translation.manual.dashboard_text: (lv) The Dashboard provides a real-time overview of your system's health, including CPU and Memory usage, status of running resources, and recent system alerts.
lv.ts.translation.manual.vms_text: (lv) Manage bhyve virtual machines: list configured VMs, control their state (start/stop/restart), and access consoles directly from the web interface.
lv.ts.translation.manual.containers_text: (lv) Monitor and manage OCI-compliant containers (Docker/Podman): view resource consumption and perform basic lifecycle operations.
lv.ts.translation.manual.jails_text: (lv) Manage native FreeBSD Jails: view all active and inactive Jails, and monitor resource isolation.
lv.ts.translation.manual.cluster_text: (lv) The Cluster view allows you to manage multiple nodes within your CloudBSD infrastructure, providing a unified view of resource distribution.
lv.ts.translation.manual.network_map_text: (lv) The Network Map provides a visual representation of your infrastructure's networking, including connections between hosts, VMs, and containers.
lv.ts.translation.manual.roles_admin: (lv) Admin: Full access to all features, including user management and system configuration.
lv.ts.translation.manual.roles_operator: (lv) Operator: Can manage resources (VMs, Containers, Jails) but cannot manage users.
lv.ts.translation.manual.roles_viewer: (lv) Viewer: Read-only access to resources and system stats.
lv.ts.translation.manual.user_management_text: (lv) Administrators can create, edit, and delete users, and assign permissions.
lv.ts.translation.manual.logs_text: (lv) The Logs page provides a searchable audit trail of system activities.
lv.ts.translation.manual.settings_text: (lv) Change user profile information, update language preference, and toggle system settings.
lv.ts.translation.manual.trouble_auth: (lv) Authentication fails: Check configuration for JWT secret keys and ensure the database file is writable.
lv.ts.translation.manual.trouble_lang: (lv) Language not changing: Ensure your browser's local storage is not blocked.
lv.ts.translation.resource_list.delete_confirm: (lv) Are you sure you want to delete this {{resource}}?

zh.ts.translation.manual.title: (zh) CloudBSD Admin Web UI - User Manual
zh.ts.translation.manual.intro_text: (zh) CloudBSD Admin Web UI is a modern, responsive interface designed for managing infrastructure on FreeBSD and other CloudBSD-compatible systems. It provides a centralized dashboard for monitoring and controlling Virtual Machines (bhyve), OCI-compliant containers, and native FreeBSD Jails.
zh.ts.translation.manual.login_text: (zh) Access the UI at your configured port. Default credentials are admin/admin. It is highly recommended to change the admin password or create a new admin user immediately after first login.
zh.ts.translation.manual.language_text: (zh) On the login page, you can select your preferred language from a dropdown menu in the footer. Your language choice is persisted to your user profile once logged in.
zh.ts.translation.manual.dashboard_text: (zh) The Dashboard provides a real-time overview of your system's health, including CPU and Memory usage, status of running resources, and recent system alerts.
zh.ts.translation.manual.vms_text: (zh) Manage bhyve virtual machines: list configured VMs, control their state (start/stop/restart), and access consoles directly from the web interface.
zh.ts.translation.manual.containers_text: (zh) Monitor and manage OCI-compliant containers (Docker/Podman): view resource consumption and perform basic lifecycle operations.
zh.ts.translation.manual.jails_text: (zh) Manage native FreeBSD Jails: view all active and inactive Jails, and monitor resource isolation.
zh.ts.translation.manual.cluster_text: (zh) The Cluster view allows you to manage multiple nodes within your CloudBSD infrastructure, providing a unified view of resource distribution.
zh.ts.translation.manual.network_map_text: (zh) The Network Map provides a visual representation of your infrastructure's networking, including connections between hosts, VMs, and containers.
zh.ts.translation.manual.roles_admin: (zh) Admin: Full access to all features, including user management and system configuration.
zh.ts.translation.manual.roles_operator: (zh) Operator: Can manage resources (VMs, Containers, Jails) but cannot manage users.
zh.ts.translation.manual.roles_viewer: (zh) Viewer: Read-only access to resources and system stats.
zh.ts.translation.manual.user_management_text: (zh) Administrators can create, edit, and delete users, and assign permissions.
zh.ts.translation.manual.logs_text: (zh) The Logs page provides a searchable audit trail of system activities.
zh.ts.translation.manual.settings_text: (zh) Change user profile information, update language preference, and toggle system settings.
zh.ts.translation.manual.trouble_auth: (zh) Authentication fails: Check configuration for JWT secret keys and ensure the database file is writable.
zh.ts.translation.manual.trouble_lang: (zh) Language not changing: Ensure your browser's local storage is not blocked.
